measurements.name: New Guinea Coastal Current
measurements.source_citation: Radenac, M.-H., Leger, F., Messie, M., Dutrieux, P., Menkes, C. and Eldin, G. (2016), Wind-driven changes of surface current, temperature, and chlorophyll observed by satellites north of New Guinea, JGR Oceans 121, 2231-2252, doi:10.1002/2015JC011438.
measurements.source_locator: Section 5.1 and Figure 10, printed p2242 / retained PDF13; seasonal climatology section 5 printed p2240 / PDF11; altimetry methods printed pp2235-2236 / PDF6-7.
measurements.extraction_method: Author prose values transcribed from visually reviewed original. No velocity/SST edges digitized and no averaging of regional descriptors.
measurements.section_orientation: Author along-track regional surface descriptions; nearly coast-normal satellite tracks, with no flow-normal correction or paired coordinates independently reconstructed.
measurements.layer: Surface altimetric current anomaly or SST-associated surface water-mass vein, depending on metric. No uniform depth slab; 50-100 m upwelling and deeper NGCUC support not transferred.
measurements.time_convention: Trade-wind / austral-winter context. Section 5 describes 2001-2010 reconstructed monthly climatology with 150-500 day seasonal signals; Figure 10 illustrates August and February. These regional widths are winter descriptors illustrated in August, not widths dated for every winter month or individual year.
measurements.boundary_rule: Author-described surface vein span. Exact seasonal velocity-anomaly threshold and paired geographic edges not specified in this descriptor. Figure 3 half-maximum anomaly-standard-deviation region is a different operator.
measurements.source_quality_note: Complete unchanged HAL deposit inspected. Author regional numbers retained with their metrics and seasonal context; paired boundaries and numeric errors not recovered.
remaining_gates: Recover compatible surface current and SST boundary criteria before physical comparison.
Recover repeated matching sections before annual extrema or seasonal width geometry.
measurements.geographic_scope: Surface current-anomaly vein east of Vitiaz Strait, near southern New Britain; excludes the strait itself.
measurements.range_interpretation: Author approximate regional point descriptor; numeric uncertainty and annual variation unknown.

original_regional_context.source_cruise_season_label_conflict: Section 2.2 pairs trade winds with Dec-Feb and northwest monsoon with Jun-Sep, opposite sections 1/5 narrative. These cruise labels are not used to date the width descriptors.
original_regional_context.display_aria_label: East of Vitiaz Strait / track 099: approximately 120 km, author trade-wind surface current-anomaly vein descriptor. No midpoint, annual extrema, mapped edges or numerical uncertainty supplied.
original_regional_context.display_caption: East of Vitiaz Strait / track 099: approximately 120 km. Trade-wind / austral-winter description, illustrated by August seasonal fields. Current-anomaly vein, not full-depth or instantaneous current width.
original_regional_context.display_method_note: 2001–2010 seasonal climatology context; exact width dates, paired edges and uncertainty unresolved. Current descriptors share one source claim and overlap geographically; the near-200 km western maxima are a subset of the 100–200 km western span. Figure 3 variability-envelope widths, 80/340 km SLA smoothing, core displacement and offshore core position remain distinct metrics. No seasonal width animation inferred.
